title: Renewal true-up + multi-year uplift bands: pilot pricing framework
creator: Evan Morales
description: Purpose: define and pilot a repeatable pricing framework for renewals and expansion true-ups that (1) locks in realistic multi-year discount bands, (2) standardizes uplift rules for expansion transactions during renewal conversations, and (3) minimizes manual negotiation effort for Sales and Legal. This ticket captures product requirements, contract language candidates, billing implications, rollout plan, and the pilot cohort. It focuses on subscription/commit customers (Dedicated and Redwood Private) where true-ups and multi-year commitments drive >90% of ARR churn/expansion activity.
background: Current state: pricing support for renewals is ad hoc. Sales frequently negotiates bespoke multi-year discounts and ad-hoc uplift credits during true-ups. Billing and Revenue Ops must handle complex pro-rates and mid-term adjustments. Consequence: longer sales cycles, inconsistent margin erosion, hard-to-forecast revenue and SLO mismatch. Goal: create a concise set of bands and rules that Sales can apply without Legal rework for most customers, and an escalation path when exceptions exceed thresholds.
success_metrics: Reduction in time-to-close renewal deals by 20% within pilot cohort
Increase in net dollar retention (NDR) by +4 percentage points for pilot cohort at next renewal
Decrease in custom contract exceptions submitted to Legal by 60%
Billing reconciliation errors related to true-ups reduced to <1% of invoices for pilot customers
proposed_pricing_model: True-up cadence: quarterly lookback for usage variance; annual contract true-up by default at renewal unless customer opts into quarterly true-up in their contract
Multi-year discount matrix: 12-month = baseline (0% uplift), 24-month = 6% discount, 36-month = 10% discount off list, with floor price defined per model family

Uplift rules on expansion: automated uplift percentage based on expansion size: 0-20% expansion = no uplift, 21-50% = +3% uplift, >50% = +7% uplift applied to new committed baseline; uplift caps at 12% without Legal approval
True-up rounding: invoiceable true-up amounts rounded to nearest $100 for customers >$50k ARR, nearest $10 for smaller accounts to reduce micro-invoices
Early-exit/termination treatment: multi-year discounts recouped on pro-rated basis if Customer terminates early per contract clause drafted below
contract_language_snippets: True-Up: Customer agrees to a periodic reconciliation of actual usage against committed units. Unless Customer elects quarterly reconciliation, the parties will perform an annual true-up at each anniversary where Customer will be invoiced or credited for the delta in accordance with the rates set forth in the Order Form.

Multi-Year Discount: Customer receives a one-time term discount for committing to a 24- or 36-month term. Discount percentages are defined in the Order Form and apply to recurring base subscription charges only; professional services, overages, and third-party pass-through costs are excluded.

Expansion Uplift: Increases in committed capacity during the Term may be subject to an uplift adjustment as set forth in the Order Form. The Sales representative must follow the standard uplift matrix; exceptions greater than the defined cap require Legal & RevOps approval.
billing_implications: RevOps must support automated proration for mid-term expansions and apply uplift percentages at invoice generation time
Stripe/Billing system: new billing event types for 'true-up invoice' vs 'order-form adjustment' to allow reconciliation and tagging in accounting exports
Revenue recognition: true-up invoices recognized as catch-up revenue; multi-year discounts amortized over the contract term per accounting guidance
Edge case: customers moving from metered to committed tiers require logic to carry forward existing KV cache pricing tiers and apply any quoted discount to new baseline
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Mar 2026): finalize matrix, legal snippets, and enablement doc; sign-off from Finance and Legal
Phase 1 pilot (Apr-May 2026): run pilot with 3 mid-market accounts (target ARR $80k-$250k) picked with AMs; use standard Order Form with 'pilot pricing band' clause toggle
Phase 2 (Jun 2026): expand to 15 accounts and enable RevOps automation for invoice tagging; collect metrics
Phase 3 (Jul-Aug 2026): iterate on uplift percentages based on pilot outcomes; prepare for platform-wide rollout (billing-2026-Q2)

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales will request larger-than-planned discounts to close renewals. Mitigation: enforce clear escalation path, pre-approved exception thresholds, and quota credit rules for SDR/AE compensation.
Risk: Billing automation gaps causing incorrect invoices. Mitigation: manual verification step for pilot invoices and a dedicated RevOps runbook for reconciliation.
Risk: Accounting complexity on amortization. Mitigation: Finance to sign-off on accounting treatment and RevOps to produce sample journal entries prior to pilot.
Risk: Customers push back on uplift rules. Mitigation: include customer-friendly language in Order Form and pilot with accounts that have trusted relationships with their AMs.
decisions_to_make: Decide whether quarterly true-ups should be opt-in or opt-out for customers under $100k ARR
Agree on rounding thresholds for invoiceable true-up deltas
Confirm whether discounts apply to add-on SKUs and overages
